name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 21 points Republican, among the most GOP-favorable in the country
Ezell holds an overwhelming fundraising edge, roughly $990,000 to $29,000 for Hulum
Prediction markets price a Democratic upset at only about 3%
No public polls or expert ratings; independent Boyanton also on the ballot
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Republican lean, Ezell's renomination and lopsided financial advantage, and market pricing near 96% Republican all point the same direction, and no polling contradicts them; the race stays safely Republican with an expected margin near 19 points.
model.watch: Any late poll showing a single-digit contest or significant outside spending against Ezell would be the signal to revisit, though nothing currently points to one.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 4th District leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of about 21 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Ezell secured renomination and enters the general election as a strong favorite. Democratic challenger Jeffrey Hulum III has raised roughly $29,000 against Ezell's near-$1 million, and independent Carl Boyanton is also on the ballot, though his fundraising is modest as well.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets give Republicans about a 96% chance of holding the seat. The combination of a deep-red electorate, an established incumbent, and a lopsided financial gap leaves Democrats with little apparent path; the realistic question is the size of the winning margin, not which party prevails.
